scope: Same 600-step physical task, Re calibration, Qc shape, Qe shape, P0 and acceptance gates. Optional offline tuner, not a browser solver or hardware controller.
commonInitialization: All four existing pair baselines at effort=1, process=1, MPC horizon=30 evaluated on all three training instances; 12 evaluations count against every method's budget. No other historical outcomes are loaded.

loss.formula: 16*hardFailure + 4*taskFailure + completedTaskScore/512. Each completed score is checked <=512, never clipped. Over the same 3 instances the mean preserves hard-count, task-count, task-score ordering. Partial racing comparisons are not complete-set certificates.

finalSelection.validation: Reevaluate shortlist plus baseline on all three fixed validation instances; choose minimum task score among fully successful candidates, with the original 1% simplicity policy. No test-driven reselection.

testConstruction: Keep six previous test scenario/initial/goal/push templates in their original order; replace each seed with the three seeds in the matching row. Four primary templates x3=12, two boundary templates x3=6. All optimization and validation locks complete before any fresh test evaluation.

statistics.unit: optimizer-seed-level mean on a fixed common test panel; 600 serial frames are never independent replicates. Conditional pilot intervals, not universal superiority or failure-probability certification.

successClaim: Do not infer benefit from early rediscovery of the shared baseline. Report equally budgeted score/feasibility, certified incumbent curves, objective calls, actual model steps, tuner overhead and total measured wall cost. Report worse/unchanged outcomes and do not automatically promote any result.
execution: Every evaluation uses actual existing MuJoCo WASM and the same task runner. No cross-method cache. Grid216 is an additional finite reference, not a continuous-domain global optimum. Known training/validation templates are development data; new seeds alone do not validate a new physical domain.
excluded: no shortened rollouts or sample-period changes as fidelity
no hidden constraint relaxation or unverified command
no default replacement or automatic adoption
